## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

The reflow ovens must be switched **off** rather than left in standby because a standby oven still draws a large load: it runs at **36% of its 70 kW rating, i.e. 25.2 kW**, for as long as it stays on, while producing nothing. A properly switched-off oven only uses about **340–350 kWh per oven-weekend** (the ~30-minute post-line heat-up plus residual), whereas leaving it in standby burns continuous power all weekend. The ovens should stay on only 30 minutes after the line stops, then be switched off once no boards are inside.

## Excess energy in incident S5

During incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), **RF-02 was left in standby all weekend**:

- Weekend energy: **~1,556 kWh** vs. **~346 kWh** normal
- Excess: **~1,210 kWh** from that single oven

This is confirmed by the meter data, where RF-02 drew **1,976.9 kWh** over the period (the largest single load on the SMT feeder MDB-1), far above the other ovens (RF-01: 1,068.7 kWh, RF-03: 334.9 kWh).

answer:
According to the demand-exceedance procedure, here is the shedding order:

## First load shed

**EV charging (EV-01)** is shed first — it can be paused 100% and has no effect on production, so it is the least disruptive action. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

The full shed sequence (least to most disruptive) is:
1. **Pause EV charging** — EV-01 (100%)
2. **Delay the next burn-in loading** — BI-01, BI-02 (35%)
3. **Raise chilled-water setpoint +1 °C** — CH-01, CH-02 (4%)
4. **Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar** — AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 (3.5%)

[source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

## Loads that must NEVER be shed

- **Server room (DC-01)** — a continuous critical load, never part of any load-shed action [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
- **Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04)** [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
- **Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03)** [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

Restoration is done in reverse order once demand is stable and below the 1,125 kW warning line: pressure, setpoint, burn-in loading, then EV charging — not all at once. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 5: restore]
